title: Ad-hoc inference policy backtest harness (scratch)
content:
Purpose:

This is a personal scratchpad for an ad-hoc local harness to backtest inference-level routing and fallback policies against recorded traffic. The goal is a tiny, runnable tool (python CLI + small config DSL) that can:
  - ingest recorded request traces (minimal: prompt, req_meta, model_used, timestamps, response tokens)
  - apply a policy function (routing, fallback, throttling, model-variant selection) deterministically to the trace as if the policy had been active at time-of-request
  - compute cost/latency/quality delta compared to observed baseline
  - emit summary metrics and a small set of replayed example traces for qualitative check

Why: useful to validate ideas (e.g., lightweight prefix cache + cheap-variant fallback) locally before we propose experiments in Dedicated or Console rollout. Lightweight, privacy-safe by default (strip PII).

Quick ideas to capture here:
  - minimal shape so product folks can read the output: per-route N, mean latency, 95p latency, token cost delta, percentage of successful fallbacks, potential SLO violations introduced
  - policy DSL: small YAML that maps route patterns -> prioritized model list + fallback budget + prefix-cache-ttl + admission rules

Example recorded trace shape (input format we will accept) - newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) per request:
{
  "req_id": "r-20250101-001",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-01T12:34:56.123Z",
  "route": "/chat/v1",
  "prompt_tokens": 42,
  "response_tokens": 128,
  "observed_model": "redwood-7b-8k",
  "observed_latency_ms": 230,
  "metadata": {"tenant_tier": "free", "region": "us-west-2"},
  "response_digest": "sha256:..."
}

Notes: metadata should be flat key->string in the trace file (we will canonicalize). We intentionally keep no raw text to avoid PI/egregious data retention; response_digest + token counts are sufficient for cost/quality proxies.

Policy DSL sketch (YAML)
---
rules:
  - pattern: "/chat/*"
    priority_models:
      - name: "redwood-7b-8k-quant"
        max_latency_ms: 400
        cost_weight: 1.0
      - name: "redwood-3b-8k-quant"
        max_latency_ms: 200
        cost_weight: 0.6
    fallback_budget_per_minute: 20
    prefix_cache:
      ttl_seconds: 90
      max_entries: 20000
    admission_filters:
      - name: "high_cost_override"
        min_response_tokens: 200
---

Interpretation: for a request that matches pattern, the policy tries the first model; if latency/capacity constraints would be violated, it considers lower-cost model variants subject to fallback_budget. prefix_cache TTL is used to simulate prefix cache hits: if request prompt_digest exists, treat response as cache-hit with near-zero latency and negligible cost.

Policy function pseudo-API (how harness will call it):
  decide_model(request_trace, policy_state) -> (chosen_model, simulated_latency_ms, used_cache_bool, fallback_reason_opt)

We will implement decision function in python (deterministic RNG seed optional) and keep policy_state small: per-minute fallback counters, prefix cache index (in-memory set of digests), model queue utilization sketch. No external services.

Quality proxies:
  - response_digest match rate: if chosen_model != observed_model, check if any baseline A/B experiments exist. Absent ground truth, treat digest mismatch as unknown; we track digest-change-rate as proxy for quality regression.
  - token-count-derived cost: cost = (prompt_tokens + response_tokens) * model_unit_price (configurable in policy file). We'll include parameterized unit_price per model.

ASCII diagram of replay flow:

  [ndjson traces] -> [replay CLI] -> [parse + normalize] -> [policy engine] -> [simulator: (latency model + cost calc + cache sim)] -> [metrics aggregator] -> [report.json + examples.ndjson]

Simulated latency model notes:
  - baseline: observed_latency_ms is carried forward if chosen_model == observed_model and no cache hit
  - fallback/cold-start penalty: switching to a different model may add extra cold_ms (configurable)
  - cache hit latency: ~10ms
  - model variant latency estimate: per-model mean latency table provided in policy file (calibrated from small profiler runs)

Local run example (python CLI):
  python replay.py 
    --traces traces/2025-01-01.ndjson 
    --policy policies/cheap-fallback.yaml 
    --out reports/report-20250101.json 
    --examples reports/sampled-examples.ndjson 
    --seed 42

Output report shape (json summary):
{
  "policy_name": "cheap-fallback-jan",
  "n_requests": 6234,
  "metrics": {
    "cost_delta_usd": -12.34,
    "p95_latency_delta_ms": 45,
    "fallback_rate_pct": 8.2,
    "cache_hit_pct": 12.1
  },
  "per_route": [ {"route": "/chat/v1", "n": 4321, "cost_delta_usd": -10.1} ]
}

Experiments to add (short list):
  - calibrate per-model latency table using small synthetic runner against Dedicated dev pool (script: scripts/calibrate_latency.py)
  - implement a simple quality oracle: sample 1% of cases where chosen_model != observed_model and run a quick similarity check with open-model small-text-sim embedding to get a quality delta estimate
  - integrate optional tokenized prompt-size guard to prevent switching away for long-form outputs

Open questions / TODOs:
  - how aggressive should fallback_budget_per_minute be for enterprise tenants? tie to tenant commitments? (ask Product)
  - should we support soft-routed hybrid (prefix-cache bypass + speculative warmup) in this harness or leave to full runtime? prefer incremental: phase 1 = no speculative warmup
  - privacy: do we need to strip any metadata beyond digests to be safe for internal sharing? probably yes; follow SRE data handling checklist
  - sample size: recommend running replay on 7 days of random traffic or 1 day but multiple runs with different seeds

Quick TODOs for me:
  - [ ] wire up ndjson parser + canonicalizer (normalize route patterns, flatten metadata)
  - [ ] implement policy YAML parser + model table loader
  - [ ] simple in-memory prefix cache (LRU, TTL)
  - [ ] CLI + report emitter + smoke tests (small fixture traces)
  - [ ] push small README + one sample policy to GH draft PR

Notes to self: keep the tool intentionally tiny. The point is quick iteration, not production-grade orchestration. When an idea looks promising, we can translate the policy DSL into a Console rollout plan and a Dedicated testbed experiment.

End of scratchpad.
